metadata.description: Canonical CS ontology entries for DBMS concepts.
sources: Database System Concepts – Silberschatz et al.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A description of a relation (table) including its name, attributes, and their domains.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: The process of organising database attributes to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a database table.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A column that establishes a link between two tables by referencing the primary key of another table.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A sequence of database operations treated as a single unit that satisfies ACID properties.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A set of properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) that guarantee reliable transaction processing.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A logging technique where changes are written to a log before being applied to the database, enabling recovery.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A data structure technique to speed up database query retrieval operations.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: The process of selecting the most efficient execution plan for a given database query.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A SQL join that returns only rows with matching values in both tables.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A SQL join that includes all rows from one or both tables, with NULLs for non-matching rows.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A conceptual data model that describes entities, their attributes, and relationships between entities.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: Techniques to manage simultaneous database operations without conflicts.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: Defines how/when the changes made by one operation become visible to other concurrent operations.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A stored procedure that automatically executes in response to specific database events.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A precompiled set of SQL statements stored in the database and executed as a unit.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A programming technique for converting data between incompatible type systems using OOP languages.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A collection of related data stored in rows and columns in a relational database.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: An attribute or set of attributes that uniquely identifies a tuple in a relation.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A single row in a database table representing one instance of an entity.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A database object that speeds up data retrieval operations on a table.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A stored query that presents data from one or more tables as a virtual table.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: The formal description of the structure of a database including tables, columns, and constraints.

entries.label: DBMS_CONCEPT
entries.definition: A database object used to retrieve, update, and delete rows from a result set one row at a time.
